question: According to the Census 2011, which state among the seven sisters has the highest literacy rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mizoram** recorded the **highest literacy rate** among the seven sister states of Northeast India as per the **Census 2011**.
 
• The literacy rate of Mizoram stood at **91.33%**, which is significantly higher than the national average of India.
 
• This high literacy rate can be attributed to the state's emphasis on **education policies** and the active involvement of **local communities** in promoting education.
 
• The state has a well-established network of **schools and institutions**, even in remote areas.
 
• **Missionary schools** and the introduction of **universal primary education** have played a key role in improving literacy in Mizoram.
 
• English is widely used as a medium of instruction, and the state's inclination towards education has ensured better access to academic resources.
 
• Mizoram's literacy achievements reflect the state's commitment to **empowerment through education**, which has also contributed to its social development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya**__

 __
 
• **Meghalaya** had a literacy rate of **74.43%** in the Census 2011.
 
• The state is known for its rich cultural heritage and natural beauty but faces challenges like **infrastructure gaps** in remote areas, which impact education.
 
 
 
• **Manipur**__
 __
 
• The literacy rate of **Manipur** as per Census 2011 was **76.94%**.
 
• Manipur has shown consistent progress in education, but **geographical constraints** make access to schooling difficult in some regions.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland**__
 
 
• **Nagaland** achieved a literacy rate of **79.55%** in Census 2011.
 
• The state places emphasis on **vocational training** alongside formal education to cater to local employment needs.
